text:
Brief for Team TS3012 before meeting TS3012d (based on TS3012a, TS3012b, TS3012c).

WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED (CURRENT)
- The deluxe design includes speech recognition and an LCD screen, since the team is moving toward deluxe because people want these features. [TS3012c: "That's small. So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"] [TS3012c: "I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."]
- The case is rubber for durability against falls and a spongy feel for the young target group; wood is not an option. [TS3012c: "The case, it will be the material will be rubber, suppose."] [TS3012c: "No, wood i wood's not an option. Well it it's stylish, but we can yeah, but you can change your covers anyway."]
- The product keeps focusing on younger people as the main goal. [TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal."]
- Energy source is regular batteries; kinetic and solar options were dropped and no rechargeable module is offered. [TS3012c: "Uh energy, we choose regular regular batteries. The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features."] [TS3012c: "Well, mm it's not in the list. So we cannot choose from it. So"]
- The lost-remote recovery feature is a beep triggered from the TV plus a flashing light. [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."] [TS3012b: "the beep is a very simple thing to imple implement, just make a button on your T_V_ and just hit the button, it beeps somewhere."]
- The scroll-wheel is cancelled by vote, and channel selection uses push-buttons instead. [TS3012c: "No r no scroll-wheel. Okay. Um I don't see anything missing really."] [TS3012c: "I think a push-button for channel would be better."]
- The teletext button stays as a less prominent extra key next to mute. [TS3012c: "The left one is teletext and the right one is mute."]
- The remote has a leaner shape with softened corners and a rounded top, and the chip must be advanced to support the LCD and advanced features. [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that."] [TS3012c: "The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features."]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- Speech recognition was first rejected for memory, maturity and multi-language reasons, but is now included in the deluxe design because the new component is small and people want it. [TS3012b: "I don't think it should be implemented in a remote control yet uh."] [TS3012c: "That's small. So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"]
- The LCD screen moved from a conditional proposal (if affordable) to being included in the deluxe edition because customers want it. [TS3012b: "if it's not too expensive, we should include it"] [TS3012c: "I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."]
- Changeable covers moved from a proposed separately sold basic remote to not being part of the basic design, possibly added later for fashion. [TS3012b: "So you don't have to I think you don't have to make entire remote controls."] [TS3012c: "If we wanna expand our options, f be fashionable, then we can get changeable covers."]
- The lost-remote feature was extended from a proposed flashing LED for deaf users to a beep plus flashing light that is now implemented. [TS3012b: "Perhaps we should also make uh something like a flash on it, if you if it's lost, for people that are deaf."] [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."]
- Advanced functions moved from a second-level menu proposal to navigation through the LCD screen menu, with no button per function. [TS3012b: "maybe a second second level menu for the advanced things."] [TS3012c: "the advanced option could also be integrated in the L_C_D_ screen, of course, because you don't have to have a button for everything."]
- The remote shape changed from a distinct, curvier proposal to a leaner shape with softened corners and a rounded top. [TS3012b: "I think it should be a little distinct from everything else"] [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that."]

OPEN ACTIONS AND OWNERS
- Speaker D (Marketing Expert) will look up the exact percentage of people who want voice recognition. [TS3012c: "Yeah. Mean of uh seventy percent I think. Uh I'm I have to look it up."]
- Speaker B and Speaker C work together on the final internal and external design, and Speaker D finds out how the product will fall into the market. [TS3012c: "apparently you guys, you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design."]
- Speaker A (Project Manager) will research whether the remote can open the TV's menu, since menu buttons are shared between brands. [TS3012b: "we need to put some research into that if if we can open the menu"]
- Speaker C (Industrial Designer) will find out whether a docking or recharging solution is possible and what it costs. [TS3012b: "Yes. I'm going to try to find that out."]
- Speaker C (Industrial Designer) is studying materials for cost, with standard fibreglass circuit board and copper wiring assumed. [TS3012b: "Uh material study, I'm working on that um for the the costs."]
- Speaker D (Marketing Expert) has ideas to work on individually before the next meeting. [TS3012a: "Um no, not really yet, but I've some ideas and I will uh"]
- Everyone should propose a name for the product rather than a serial number. [TS3012b: "let's give this uh a name, and not like some vague serial number that no one understands"]

DISAGREEMENTS AND QUESTIONS STILL OPEN
- The colour and slogan are unsettled: C wants a yellow remote with black buttons, B prefers a neutral base because of covers, and A leans to black and yellow company colours. [TS3012c: "It's either black cover with yellow buttons or vice versa."]
- Where to place the speech recognition microphone (top, side, or double) is open, and the transmitter location may cause interference. [TS3012c: "Um yeah, it could be either be here or make a double microphone."]
- Whether customers want a rechargeable battery, and would pay extra for it, still needs to be found out. [TS3012b: "I'm not sure, you should find out if it's if rechargeable is important."]
- A rejects the kinetic energy option because remotes lie still most of the time and generate too little power. [TS3012c: "I'm sure t I mean remotes lie still I think like ninety nine percent of the time."]
- The selling price target is constrained because the budget is limited, according to the User Interface Designer. [TS3012a: "Okay, well that's not that much to work with."]
- Whether disabled users should be able to use the remote is unresolved; Mark thinks it should be considered, though truly disabled users might be a problem. [TS3012a: "Do we want people who are disabled in any way to uh, yeah, to be able to use it as well?"]
